data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
data.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Objective
data.text: Explore the formation of anti-glucagon antibodies to glucagon

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Recovery Objective
data.text: To evaluate the recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia

data.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
data.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
data.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs), vital signs

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
data.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
data.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

data.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand: Non-inferiority of LY900018 vs IMG for Treatment Success
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia and complete both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome. Patients are excluded if the lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, or if they receive an external measure to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, who complete both treatment visits with evaluable primary outcome (Per-Protocol completers for primary analysis)) Summary measure: Difference in percentage of treatment successes between treatment groups (IMG minus LY900018); non-inferiority declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval of the paired difference is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%. The 95% CI is obtained from the 1-sample mean of the paired differences in primary outcome (1=outcome observed; 0=outcome not observed) across 2 treatment visits..

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose before or within 10 minutes of glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives an external measure (e.g., IV glucose infusion) to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration, which would confound the assessment of glucagon treatment success.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration (beyond the first 10 minutes) to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia; data collected after IV glucose infusion may be excluded from efficacy analyses.

intercurrentEvents.name: Non-evaluable primary outcome due to insufficient hypoglycemia induction
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has at least one treatment visit in which the lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable as hypoglycemia was not adequately induced.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of both treatment periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason (e.g., adverse event, withdrawal of consent, protocol deviation), resulting in missing primary outcome data for one or both periods.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single intranasal dose by study site personnel compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, who complete both treatment visits with evaluable primary outcome (Per-Protocol completers for primary analysis)
data.variableOfInterest: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in plasma glucose (PG) to ≥70 mg/dL or an increase of ≥20 mg/dL from PG nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon, without receiving additional treatments to increase PG. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.
data.summaryMeasure: Difference in percentage of treatment successes between treatment groups (IMG minus LY900018); non-inferiority declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval of the paired difference is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%. The 95% CI is obtained from the 1-sample mean of the paired differences in primary outcome (1=outcome observed; 0=outcome not observed) across 2 treatment visits.

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: All enrolled Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who received at least one dose of study treatment, regardless of whether they completed all protocol requirements. (Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts and percentages of patients with SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term, summarized by treatment group; severity and investigator-assessed relationship to investigational product reported. Nasal/respiratory and anosmia AEs identified using preferred terms and summarized by treatment group..

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study participation due to an adverse event prior to completing all safety assessments.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of concomitant medications for AE management
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives concomitant medications (e.g., antiemetics for nausea/vomiting) to manage treatment-emergent adverse events during the study period.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion or other rescue intervention
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other rescue intervention during the hypoglycemia induction procedure, which may affect the safety profile observed.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single intranasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements
data.variableOfInterest: Incidence and severity of serious adverse events (SAEs), treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs, and changes in vital signs following single-dose administration of glucagon.
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts and percentages of patients with SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term, summarized by treatment group; severity and investigator-assessed relationship to investigational product reported. Nasal/respiratory and anosmia AEs identified using preferred terms and summarized by treatment group.

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PK samples. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with sufficient PK sampling data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) of PK parameters by treatment group; PK parameters compared between LY900018 and IMG using standard non-compartmental analysis methods in a crossover design..

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or insufficient PK blood samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing or insufficient blood samples for PK analysis due to sampling errors, hemolysis, or other technical issues, resulting in inability to derive reliable PK parameters.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion affecting glucagon PK
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion during the PK sampling window, which may affect glucagon concentration measurements and PK parameter derivation.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PK sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or leaves the clinical research unit before completion of the 4-hour PK blood sampling schedule.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single intranasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with sufficient PK sampling data
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacokinetic parameters derived from serial blood sampling for glucagon concentrations collected immediately before and up to 4 hours following glucagon administration, including area under the concentration-time curve (AUC), maximum observed concentration (Cmax), and time to maximum concentration (Tmax).
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) of PK parameters by treatment group; PK parameters compared between LY900018 and IMG using standard non-compartmental analysis methods in a crossover design.

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD (plasma glucose) measurements. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of PD parameters (BGmax and Tmax) by treatment group; absolute change from baseline in PG values at various post-dose time points summarized by treatment group..

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other intervention to raise PG concentration after glucagon administration; measurements taken after the time of intervention will be excluded from PD analysis.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge
intercurrentEvents.text: All patients receive a carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge from the clinical research unit, which may affect late post-dose plasma glucose measurements.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or insufficient PD plasma glucose samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing or insufficient plasma glucose measurements for PD analysis due to sampling errors or early discontinuation from the clinical research unit.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single intranasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD data
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacodynamic parameters derived from serial plasma glucose (PG) concentration measurements collected immediately before and up to 4 hours following glucagon administration, including maximum plasma glucose concentration (BGmax) and time to maximum plasma glucose concentration (Tmax).
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of PD parameters (BGmax and Tmax) by treatment group; absolute change from baseline in PG values at various post-dose time points summarized by treatment group.

data.name: Exploratory Anti-Glucagon Antibody Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of LY900018 or IMG, with available blood samples for anti-glucagon antibody assessment at baseline and follow-up. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable antibody samples) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts and percentages of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies at baseline and post-dose, summarized by treatment group..

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing follow-up antibody sample
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not attend the follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after last study treatment) or has insufficient sample for anti-glucagon antibody assessment.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before follow-up visit
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient withdraws from the study or is lost to follow-up before the scheduled antibody assessment at the follow-up visit.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single intranasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen) administered as a single IM injection
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable antibody samples
data.variableOfInterest: Presence of anti-glucagon antibodies assessed at baseline and at the follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after the last study treatment) to explore immunogenicity following single-dose administration of glucagon.
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts and percentages of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies at baseline and post-dose, summarized by treatment group.

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Symptoms Recovery Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product, with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable symptom questionnaire data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale at baseline and various post-dose time points, and absolute change from baseline, summarized by treatment group..

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other rescue intervention to raise PG concentration, which may affect the patient's hypoglycemia symptom experience and questionnaire responses.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient is unable to complete the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale questionnaire at one or more time points due to severe hypoglycemia symptoms, early discharge, or other reasons.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before symptom assessment completion
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or leaves the clinical research unit before completing all scheduled hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire assessments.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single intranasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable symptom questionnaire data
data.variableOfInterest: Recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia assessed using the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale questionnaire, including total score and each subscale score at baseline and various post-dose time points following glucagon administration.
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale at baseline and various post-dose time points, and absolute change from baseline, summarized by treatment group.
